Key reference document is NIST AI 100-5e2025 (Plan for Global Engagement on AI Standards).

documents.title: From Principles to Practice | OSTP | The White House
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: This is a non-binding technical companion to the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights. It provides illustrative examples and practical steps but explicitly states expectations are a 'blueprint for the development of additional technical standards' rather than enforceable rules. Reporting expectations are directed at entities developing or using automated systems but are voluntary. The document covers five principles intended to guide design, use, and deployment of automated systems.

documents.title: Roadmap for the NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) | NIST
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: This Roadmap is a companion to AI RMF 1.0, voluntary and non-sector specific. Key priorities include international standards alignment, expanded TEVV efforts, AI RMF profiles, guidance on trustworthiness tradeoffs, measuring framework effectiveness, case studies, human factors guidance, explainability guidance, risk tolerance methods, and multi-disciplinary tutorials. NIST's involvement depends on available resources.

documents.title: AI Risk Management Framework: Initial Draft - March 17, 2022
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: This is the first draft of the NIST AI RMF, published March 17, 2022. Part 3 was not yet developed at time of publication. The framework is explicitly voluntary and not a compliance mechanism; it is intended to be used alongside existing laws, regulations, and mandatory guidance. Developed under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283). Framework covers all sectors, organization sizes, and AI maturity levels.

documents.title: AI Risk Management Framework: Second Draft - August 18, 2022
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: The AI RMF is explicitly voluntary and law- and regulation-agnostic. It is not a compliance mechanism and not intended to supersede existing regulations or laws. An accompanying NIST AI RMF Playbook provides suggested tactical actions. The framework is structured around four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: The AI RMF is explicitly voluntary: 'Like the AI RMF, the Playbook is voluntary and organizations can utilize the suggestions according to their needs and interests.' It does not prescribe risk tolerance and is intended to be flexible and to augment existing risk practices. It provides four core functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE. No penalties or enforcement mechanisms are established.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: NIST AI 600-1 is explicitly voluntary guidance serving as a companion to AI RMF 1.0, developed per EO 14110 Section 4.1(a)(i)(A). It provides suggested (not required) actions organized by AI RMF functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage). Four primary GAI considerations are addressed: Governance, Pre-Deployment Testing, Content Provenance, and Incident Disclosure. The document covers general-purpose/foundation models broadly across sectors. No binding enforcement mechanisms are created by this document itself; references to mandatory reporting (e.g., HIPAA) point to pre-existing external legal obligations rather than new requirements from this profile.

documents.title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-03: Adverse action notification requirements in connection with credit decisions based on complex algorithms
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: This circular is explicitly a 'general statement of policy under the Administrative Procedure Act' and does not impose new legal requirements but clarifies that existing ECOA/Regulation B obligations apply to AI/ML-based credit decisions. Enforcement is shared across CFPB, state AGs, prudential regulators, and other federal agencies. Confidence reflects that the underlying legal obligations are binding, though the circular itself is not binding law.

documents.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions
findings: title or notes indicate a substantive policy instrument
documents.analysis_notes: This is nonbinding regulatory guidance issued under FD&C Act Section 515C (added by FDORA 2022). It provides recommendations for PCCPs in marketing submissions for AI-enabled device software functions (AI-DSFs). The guidance is not legally enforceable on its own but operationalizes statutory requirements for PMA, 510(k), and De Novo pathways. Covered domains are primarily healthcare/medical devices. The guidance emphasizes that 'should' language is recommended but not required. Deviations from an authorized PCCP, however, may trigger statutory adulteration/misbranding consequences. QSR (21 CFR Part 820) compliance is mandatory and integral to PCCP implementation. Early FDA engagement via Q-Submission Program is strongly encouraged, especially for high-risk or combination product devices.
